html:
The Maputo Protocol is a treaty of the African Union on the rights of women, adopted in Maputo, the capital of Mozambique, in July 2003. It came into force in 2005.

Its full name is the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa. It adds to the African Charter of 1981 and covers a wide range of rights:

  • equal rights in marriage, divorce and inheritance, and a minimum marriage age of 18;
  • political participation and equal pay;
  • protection from violence, including a call to ban female genital mutilation;
  • health and reproductive rights.

Article 14 made it the first international treaty to call for legal abortion in some cases, such as rape, incest, or danger to the mother's life or health. That clause made it controversial with churches and some governments.

Most African Union members have ratified it, though several still have not, and many that did have been slow to change their laws. Women's groups use it in courts and campaigns as a yardstick.
sum: The Maputo Protocol is a treaty of the African Union on the rights of women, adopted in Maputo, the capital of Mozambique, in July 2003. It came into force in 2005.
